architecture.mechanism: Integration of intelligent algorithms into modified heating, ventilation and air conditioning architectures with evaporator coils beneath seat surfaces for direct two-way thermal management.
architecture.intervention: Install evaporator coils beneath the engine seat mounting surfaces and integrate an Artificial Neural Network control unit to manage two-way heating and cooling of the engine block based on real-time thermal load predictions, reducing parasitic loss from conventional bulk fluid cooling systems.
architecture.expected_effect: Reduction in thermal and mechanical energy loss by optimizing local heat rejection only where needed, improving overall engine coefficient of performance and fuel efficiency while maintaining road-usability.
architecture.falsification_test: Operate the modified engine on a dynamometer under standard drive cycles and measure net fuel consumption; if the specific fuel consumption increases by more than 2% compared to the baseline conventional cooling system, the mechanism fails to improve efficiency.
